text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Glafcos Clerides departs for Athens today for talks with the Greek government, taking with him a document on the UN-sponsored military dialogue aimed at reducing tension between the two sides on Cyprus.
- The Supreme Court is set to decide whether discount sales in shops should be regulated by law within a specified period of time.

- Confusion reigns in government circles as to whether Clerides will run for the presidency in the elections scheduled in early 1998, while rumours abound that he plans to support the candidacy of (centre right) Diko party leader Spyros Kyprianou, a former president.

- Britain, the United Nations and the United States want a high level agreement reached between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides on Cyprus before direct talks between them are interrupted for the presidential campaign period.
- The auditor-general suggests restricting the number of duty free shops outside the island's ports, saying their presence increases the risks of smuggling.

- President Clerides goes to Athens today to discuss tactics and strategy the Greek Cypriot side will follow during the talks scheduled in New York with Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash next week.
- Residents in the towns of Limassol and Paphos waste water, while Nicosia residents have restricted water use by 23 percent.
